--client validation: AgentControlGate.clientName strips control, format (bidi), separator, private-use and unassigned scalars, collapses whitespace, and caps at 80 characters. Failures exit 2 and the sent name is the sanitized one. Tests cover the bidi, length and BEL cases.

Parser split (36c95bd): compared line by line with the pre-split parse. The order is unchanged (split, then client check, then --help, then command). The defaults (Terminal / Claude Code) and the tool names, option handling and error strings are identical. No behavior change found.
open_notes: The client name is self-asserted. Any local process can claim an already-approved name such as 'Claude Code'. This is inherited from the socket design and not new here.
The client's read loop has no timeout. This is fine because the server bounds wait at 300 s, but a hung app hangs the command.

findings.status: open (NIT, pre-existing); the server bounds waits at 300 s

verified: Descriptors are closed on every path: exchange defers close(descriptor) right after connect(to:) returns, and connect(to:) closes before each of its own throws (path too long, connect failed). Only the `socket()` failure throws without a close, and there is no descriptor then.

Name resolution is correct. `Darwin.connect` and `Darwin.socket` are qualified, so they don't collide with the static `connect(to:)`. `close`, `read`, `write` and `setsockopt` have no competing member in the enum.
SO_NOSIGPIPE is set on the descriptor before use, so a write to a closed peer gives EPIPE (mapped to Unavailable) instead of killing the command with SIGPIPE.

writeAll: it loops on partial writes with `line[sent...]` (the slice's baseAddress is correct), retries on EINTR, and throws Unavailable on 0 or an error. That is consistent with the claim that msgblast ignores a partial line.
readReply: EINTR is retried. EOF or an error before a newline throws NoReply. It returns exactly the first line plus a newline.
exchange throws NoReply only after the whole request is written, and Unavailable otherwise.
AgentControlCommand uses `catch is NoReply` and exits 6 with AgentControlCLI.noReply text; any other error exits 5. The usage text lists '6 no answer after the request was sent (it may have run)'.

Test: it first checks that a missing socket gives Unavailable. The listener binds and listens before the client connects, so the accept backlog absorbs any ordering race. The server thread reads the 3-byte request and closes, so the client sees EOF and NoReply. Cleanup closes the server and unlinks the path, and the path is well under the 104-byte sun_path limit. The Thread closure captures only a let Int32, so it is fine under Swift 6 Sendable checking. I see no flakiness.

Delta review: the base's merged fixes (socket argument guard, Settings save errors, event feed) don't touch the CLI files beyond the conflict-free merge. The whole-PR diff against the base is the CLI, command, Settings view, tests and project file, with nothing broken.
open_notes: I cannot compile here; the Swift 6 strict-concurrency reading is by inspection only. I found no compile or concurrency problems.
Exit 6 is the only status where a retry might double-run a request. The text says so, which is the right call.

verified: git diff 4ba0b09 3669eb1 --stat: only msgblastTests/AgentControlCLITests.swift changed (9 insertions, 7 deletions).

Every libc call in the socket test is now Darwin.-qualified: socket, close (x3), unlink, bind, listen, accept, read. The remaining unqualified names are sockaddr_un, sa_family_t, socklen_t, AF_UNIX and SOCK_STREAM, which are types and constants that NSObject does not shadow.
A grep of the file for other plain C calls that could collide with NSObject or XCTestCase members (sleep, exit, connect, send, write, open, select, poll, and similar) found none.
`import Darwin` before `import XCTest` is fine, and `Darwin.bind(server, $0, ...)` inside the withMemoryRebound closure resolves to the C function.
